 More than 4 million tubes of kids’ toothpaste recalled, federal regulators warn
 Recalled items include Brush Buddies’ Hot Wheels, Crayola, My Little Pony brands and more
 Jenny Sherman , Digital Content Producer
 Published:  October 26, 2026 at 12:49 PM Updated:  October 26, 2026 at 1:11 PM Tags:  FDA , Consumer Alerts , Product Recall , Recalls More than four million tubes of kids’ and adult toothpaste sold nationwide have been recalled due to “deviations” in the manufacturing process, federal regulators announced.
 According to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the recall covers various fluoride toothpaste brands featuring licensed characters geared toward children, including “Brush Buddies” Hot Wheels, Crayola, My Little Pony and Barbie toothpastes, among others, with flavors like bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon and cookies and cream.
 Related->> More than 1.5M pounds of ready-to-eat meat, poultry products recalled nationwide, USDA says 
 All the products were manufactured by India-based Pritam International Private Ltd, which voluntarily recalled the items out of an abundance of caution after the FDA flagged manufacturing problems at the facility that packaged them.
 The affected tubes have expiration dates stretching into 2028, and the recall has been designated by the FDA as a Class II, meaning there is only a moderate risk of adverse health consequences. So far, no illnesses or injuries have been reported, according to federal regulators.
 A full list of the recalled products can be found here.
